content.text: Purpose

CRUD workflow for playbooks via the Who2Be MCP write tools. Covers atomic and composite playbooks. A playbook is created as a draft and only activated after review — the draft-to-active workflow stays server-side. A composite's sub-playbook sequence is set via
set_playbook_composes
; references to knowledge resources via
set_playbook_resource_links
Identify the Mode
Create: The user wants to set up a new workflow.
Update: The user names an existing playbook plus a change.
Transition: A draft should be published (active) or an active playbook withdrawn (inactive).
Restore: An earlier version should be restored as a new draft.
Token-Saving Strategy: Reuse Before Creating New
Before EVERY new creation:

use search to look for existing playbooks with similar content and use find_usages to check where a candidate is already deployed. If a suitable playbook exists, use it as a sub-playbook (set_playbook_composes) instead of creating a duplicate — duplicates drift apart and cost tokens twice over.
Pointer embedding as the default:

link resources via set_playbook_resource_links as pointers (embedding_mode 'lazy') — the consumer loads them on demand via fetch_resource. Only use inline embedding with justification (small content needed on EVERY run).
Composite decomposition:
as soon as a workflow contains reusable sub-steps, break it into atomic sub-playbooks plus one orchestrating composite — the sub-steps can then be reused in other composites instead of being copied.
Create — Set Up a New Playbook
Phase 1 — Understand
Persona binding: Which persona uses the playbook? Does it already exist (get_persona)? If not, follow the persona playbook first and create the persona, then return here.
Type: Is the playbook atomic (a self-contained workflow, a leaf node) or a composite (orchestrates several atomic playbooks in a sequence)?

Triggers: Which user phrases activate the playbook? Format and collision cross-check (list_triggers) are mandatory per the trigger hygiene rules in the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource. Check beforehand: the Token-Saving Strategy section — does a suitable playbook already exist?
Tags: Use an existing category, or is it really a new one? Cross-check tags via list_playbooks() rather than expanding them freely.
Description: A concise one-line summary.
Resource references: Does the playbook rely on knowledge resources? If so, note the resource IDs (later set_playbook_resource_links).
For a composite: don't invent its own steps — the body describes only the orchestration; the domain steps live in the sub-playbooks. A composite only has value once it has two or more sub-playbooks.
Phase 2 — Proposal
Atomic: Draft the body as a BlockNote document — clear phases or numbered steps, plus the Tools & Operations, Anti-Patterns, and Notes sections.

Composite: Draft the body as a numbered sequence of sub-playbooks plus a sequence-discipline section (when the composite doesn't fit, what happens if a sub-playbook is missing). The order in the body is the binding source of truth.
Phase 3 — Write
create_playbook
is called with name and content (description, body as BlockNote JSON, type, tags, triggers). This creates a draft version 1 — status is server-side draft, not active.
For a composite:
set_playbook_composes
with the parent ID and the child IDs in the desired order (replace semantics). Only link active sub-playbooks.
For resource references:
set_playbook_resource_links
to set the resource links (replace semantics).
Persona binding: The M:N persona-to-playbook assignment is set on the persona side (
set_persona_playbooks
) — see the Persona playbook. A playbook without a persona hangs in a vacuum.
Phase 4 — Hand-Off
Review the playbook content with the user.
After approval, call
transition_playbook
with version=1 and to="active". Promoting to active requires the promote_retire capability.
For a composite: verify that all linked sub-playbooks exist and are active — otherwise inactive children are skipped when rendered.
Update — Change an Existing Playbook
Understand: Load the playbook with
fetch_playbook
, clarify the scope of the change — a body section (Procedure / Tools & Operations / Anti-Patterns / Notes) or a field (triggers, tags, description, type).
Propose: Consolidate the edit and align it with the user before writing.
Write:
update_playbook

with the complete content. On an active version, this creates a new draft version (no in-place edit; if a draft already exists, this returns 409). Follow up with set_playbook_composes / set_playbook_resource_links if composes or resource links need updating.

Hand-off: Switch the new draft to active via transition_playbook. For trigger changes, check whether a persona-mode trigger still refers to the old value. When switching type from atomic to composite, set the composes sequence; when switching from composite to atomic, clear it.
Transition — Publish & Withdraw
transition_playbook

with id, version, and to switches the status: draft to review, review to active, or active to inactive (withdrawn). draft/review only requires the write capability; promoting to active and retiring to inactive require promote_retire.
Before withdrawing, check inbound references: Which composites or personas use the playbook? Affected spots need adjustment — warn the user.
Status invariant: at most one version per playbook is active. Activating a new version automatically sets the old one to inactive.
Restore — Recover an Earlier Version
restore_playbook
with id and the source version copies its content as a new draft. Then review it and switch it to active via transition_playbook — never overwrite the active version directly.
Tools & Operations

Read: fetch_playbook (body + fields), list_playbooks (catalog, tags), list_triggers (check trigger collisions), search (content search before creating new), find_usages (where a playbook is already deployed).
Write: create_playbook (draft v1), update_playbook (new draft), transition_playbook (switch status), restore_playbook (old version as draft).
Linking: set_playbook_composes (a composite's sub-playbook sequence, replace semantics), set_playbook_resource_links (resource references, replace semantics).

Forbidden: no hard delete via MCP; never set composes on draft or inactive playbooks; no composite with only one sub-playbook (premature composite); don't edit personas or resources within this playbook — dedicated playbooks exist for that.
Anti-Patterns
Creating a composite without an explicit sequence-discipline section — when it doesn't fit and what applies if a sub-playbook is missing must be stated in the body.
Setting composes to non-existent or non-active playbooks — a composite only makes sense when all sub-playbooks are ready for use (active).
Forgetting the persona binding — a playbook without an assigned persona is never found by any agent.
Assigning triggers against trigger hygiene (generic single words, no comma separation, no collision cross-check) — see the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource for the canonical format.
Wanting to create directly as active — create_playbook always produces a draft; activation runs exclusively through transition_playbook.
Writing the procedure body as a loose block of prose — use numbered steps or clear phase headers.
Notes

Composite convention: The order in set_playbook_composes is the execution-relevant source of truth. When a composite is rendered, the numbered sub-playbook sequence is automatically appended to the body; inactive or missing children are skipped.
The draft-to-active workflow stays server-side: MCP write tools only create drafts; publishing always runs through transition_playbook. There is deliberately no hard delete via MCP.

Conventions: Trigger hygiene, naming, the modes rule, policy patterns, and managed boundaries are binding in the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource — look them up there instead of duplicating rules here. It is linked as a lazy pointer and does NOT come along automatically: load it via fetch_resource before Phase 2 (Proposal); the resource_id is in this playbook's linked_blocks entry.
Feedback

If you notice something outdated or incorrect while reading existing elements, report it via submit_feedback (signal outdated/incorrect/unclear) instead of silently passing over it; report used playbooks/resources via record_usage (applied/skipped/error). This is how the AgentDB becomes self-improving.
